zero_omission_notes.summary: Development encompasses material aspirations (higher income, employment) as well as non-material goals like freedom, security, equal treatment, and respect. Relying solely on per capita income (World Bank criterion) ignores income distribution and essential human indicators like literacy, life expectancy, and infant mortality, which are captured by the Human Development Index (HDI). Development must also be ecologically sustainable.

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 1.1 What Development Promises - Different People, Different Goals
detailed_sections.full_notes: Different individuals have distinct developmental aspirations depending on their socio-economic backgrounds. Goals can often be conflicting (e.g., industrialists wanting large dams for electricity vs. indigenous tribal communities losing land and livelihoods).

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Developmental Conflict Case Study
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: A urban high-rise development displacing local slum dwellers or dam construction submerging agricultural land demonstrates that what is progress for one group can be destructive for another.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Besides seeking more income, people aspire for non-material factors such as security, dignity, non-discrimination, and work-life balance. For instance, women engaging in paid work gain dignity, but safety and equal household sharing are prerequisites.
National development involves making fair and just decisions on priorities that benefit the majority of citizens rather than a select elite group.

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 1.4 How to Compare Different Countries or States?
detailed_sections.full_notes: Countries are categorized by World Bank using Per Capita Income (Total National Income divided by Total Population). High-income countries have per capita income above USD 49,300 per annum (2021), whereas low-income countries have USD 2,500 or less. India is a low-middle income country (USD 2,370 in 2021).
Comparing Indian states shows that while Haryana had higher per capita income than Kerala, Kerala surpassed Haryana in Infant Mortality Rate (IMR), Net Attendance Ratio, and Literacy Rate.
Money cannot buy a pollution-free environment, protection from infectious diseases, or community safety. Public distribution systems (PDS) and state-funded education/health infrastructure are vital.
Sustainable development ensures present growth does not compromise future generations. Examples include groundwater depletion in agricultural states and crude oil reserve depletion globally.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: The average income earned per person in a given area (country/state) in a specified year.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Calculated by dividing total national income by total population.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: The number of children that die before completing one year of age as a proportion of 1,000 live children born in that specific year.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Kerala has a low IMR due to adequate primary healthcare infrastructure.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: The proportion of literate population in the 7 and above age group.
The total number of children of age group 14 and 15 years attending school as a percentage of total number of children in the same age group.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Used to gauge secondary educational participation.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: A composite index measuring average achievement in three key dimensions: health (life expectancy), education (mean & expected years of schooling), and standard of living (GNI per capita).
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Published annually by UNDP in the Human Development Report.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: A measure of adult body fat based on weight relative to height squared.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Weight in kg divided by height in meters squared.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: Per Capita Income = Total Income of Country / Total Population of Country
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.si_unit_or_notation: Total Income = Gross National Product/Income; Total Population = Resident inhabitants
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: If a country generates $1,000,000 with 1,000 residents, PCI is $1,000.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.si_unit_or_notation: Weight in kilograms, Height in meters. BMI < 18.5 is undernourished; BMI >= 25 is overweight.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: A person weighing 50 kg with height 1.6 m has BMI = 50 / (1.6 * 1.6) = 19.53 (Normal).

textbook_exercises.question: Development of a country can generally be determined by (i) its per capita income (ii) its average literacy level (iii) health status of its people (iv) all the above
textbook_exercises.answer: Answer: (iv) all the above. Holistic development includes economic growth alongside human capital indicators.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: Which international organization publishes the Human Development Report?
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: UNDP evaluates countries using HDI metrics combining health, education, and income.

short_answer_questions.question: Why is per capita income considered an inadequate metric for comparing national development?
short_answer_questions.answer: Per capita income hides income disparities across citizens, ignores essential public goods (healthcare, safety, clean environment), and fails to measure literacy or life expectancy. Key points: Hides income distribution/disparities; Ignores health and education indicators; Excludes non-material factors

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Passage Context: ''The Earth has enough resources to meet the needs of all but not enough to satisfy the greed of even one person.' - Mahatma Gandhi' - How is this statement relevant to the discussion of development?
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: It underlines the necessity of sustainable resource utilization, warning against over-exploitation of natural assets like groundwater and fossil fuels for short-term profits.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Explain the concept of Sustainable Development. Illustrate with examples of resource depletion in India.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: Sustainable development refers to development that meets present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs. In India, groundwater over-exploitation (1/3 of districts pumping beyond recharge rates in Punjab/Western UP) and global crude oil depletion highlight the urgent need for renewable transition and regulatory enforcement.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: In a village in Tamil Nadu, 90% of rural households access subsidized food grains via PDS shops, whereas in West Bengal only 35% do.

qa.question: Which state's rural population is likely to have better health and nutritional status and why?
qa.answer: Tamil Nadu, because effective Public Distribution Systems ensure equitable access to essential nutritional requirements regardless of private income.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Equating high Per Capita Income directly with high overall development.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Always evaluate HDI parameters (IMR, Literacy, Life Expectancy) alongside per capita income. (Root Cause: Conflating economic growth with human development.)
